Commentary of al-Shawkani (*Fath al-Qadir*) on Surah 106, verses 1–4:

It is Meccan according to the majority (*al-Jumhur*).

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and al-Kalbī said: it is Medinan.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "The Surah *Li-Īlāf* was revealed in Makkah."

Al-Bukhārī in his *Tārīkh*, al-Ṭabarānī, al-Ḥākim (who authenticated it), Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqī narrated from Umm Hānī bint Abī Ṭālib that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah has favoured Quraysh with seven qualities, which He gave to no one before them and will give to no one after them: that I am among them (and in another wording: prophethood is among them), the caliphate is among them, the custodianship of the Kaʿbah (*al-Ḥijābah*) is among them, the provision of water to the pilgrims (*al-Siqāyah*) is among them, they were granted victory over the elephant, they worshipped Allah for seven years (and in another wording: ten years) when no one else worshipped Him, and a Surah of the Qurʾān was revealed about them in which no one other than them is mentioned: *Li-Īlāfi Quraysh* [that is, the Surah of Quraysh]." Ibn Kathīr said: this is a *gharīb* (a hadith narrated through a single chain at some point). Its meaning is supported by what al-Ṭabarānī in *al-Awsaṭ*, Ibn Mardawayh, and Ibn ʿAsākir narrated from al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah has favoured Quraysh with seven qualities: He favoured them in that they worshipped Allah for ten years when none worshipped Him but Quraysh; He favoured them in that He gave them victory on the Day of the Elephant while they were polytheists; He favoured them in that a Surah of the Qurʾān was revealed about them which no one of the worlds has entered other than them, and it is *Li-Īlāfi Quraysh*; and He favoured them in that prophethood, the caliphate, and the provision of water are among them."

Al-Khaṭīb in his *Tārīkh* narrated from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab a similar report, *marfūʿ* (traced directly to the Prophet ﷺ), but it is *mursal* (a report in which the Companion is omitted from the chain).

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

The *lām* in His saying ﴿*Li-Īlāfi*﴾ (for the familiarity of) is said to be connected to the end of the Surah before it, as if He, glory be to Him, said: "I destroyed the People of the Elephant for the sake of the bringing together of Quraysh."

Al-Farrāʾ said: this Surah is connected to the previous one, for He, glory be to Him, reminded the people of Makkah of His great blessing upon them in what He did to the Abyssinians. Then He said ﴿*Li-Īlāfi Quraysh*﴾, meaning: We did that to the People of the Elephant as a blessing from Us upon Quraysh. This is because Quraysh used to go out on their trade, and they were not raided in the time of ignorance (*Jāhiliyyah*), for they said: "We are the People of the House of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic." Until the owner of the Elephant came to demolish the Kaʿbah and take its stones to build with them a house in Yemen to which people would make pilgrimage; so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, destroyed them. Thus He reminded them of His blessing: that is, He did that ﴿*Li-Īlāfi Quraysh*﴾, so that they would continue to set out and no one would dare to attack them. Ibn Qutaybah mentioned something similar.

Al-Zajjāj said: the meaning is: He made them like chewed-up chaff (see 105:5) ﴿*Li-Īlāfi Quraysh*﴾, that is, Allah destroyed the People of the Elephant so that Quraysh might remain, and what they had become accustomed to of the journey of winter and summer.

Al-Zamakhsharī in *al-Kashshāf* said: the *lām* is connected to His saying ﴿*fa-l-yaʿbudū*﴾ (so let them worship), meaning: He commanded them to worship Him for the sake of their familiarity with the two journeys. The *fāʾ* (in *fa-l-yaʿbudū*) came in because the sentence carries the sense of a condition, since the meaning is: "As for whatever (it may be), let them worship Him."

Al-Khalīl ibn Aḥmad had already preceded the author of *al-Kashshāf* to this view. The meaning is: if they do not worship Him for all His other blessings, then let them worship Him for this great blessing.

Al-Kisāʾī and al-Akhfash said: the *lām* is the *lām* of wonder: that is, "Be amazed at ﴿*Li-Īlāfi Quraysh*﴾."

It is also said that it means "to" (*ilā*).

The majority of readers recited *li-īlāf*, with a *yā* and with *hamzah*, from *alifta* (ʾalifa), *yaʾlifu*, *īlāfan*.

It is said: *alifta al-shayʾ* (I was accustomed to the thing) *alafan* and *ulfan*, and *alftuhu īlāfan* has the same meaning. From it is the poet's saying:

*Those who bestow blessings when the stars have changed,*
*and those who travel on the journey of *īlāf*.*

Ibn ʿĀmir recited *li-ilāf* without the *yā*. Abū Jaʿfar recited *li-ilf*. The poet combined these two readings, saying:

*You claim that your brothers are Quraysh;*
*for them is *ilf*, and for you there is no *ilāf*.*

ʿIkrimah recited *layaʾlaf Quraysh* (let Quraysh be accustomed), with a *fatḥah* on the *lām*, taking it as the *lām* of command. It is the same in the *muṣḥaf* of Ibn Masʿūd. The *fatḥah* on the *lām* of command is a well-known dialect.

Some people of Makkah recited *ilāfu Quraysh* (with *ilāf* as a noun), and they cited the saying of Abū Ṭālib:

*He repels the people from a Hashimite band;*
*their *ilāf* among the people is the best of *ilāf*.*

Quraysh are the descendants of al-Naḍr ibn Kinānah ibn Khuzaymah ibn Mudrikah ibn Ilyās ibn Muḍar. Everyone who is a descendant of al-Naḍr is a Qurashī, and whoever is not a descendant of al-Naḍr is not a Qurashī. *Quraysh* is treated as diptote (*munṣarif*, taking nunation) if the tribe as a living group is meant, and as non-diptote (*ghayr munṣarif*, without nunation) if the tribal name is meant. From the latter is the poet's saying:

*And sufficient for Quraysh in difficult matters is its cushion.*

It is also said that Quraysh are the descendants of Fihr ibn Mālik ibn al-Naḍr, but the first view is more correct.

His saying ﴿*īlāfihim*﴾ (their familiarity) is a substitute (*badal*) for ﴿*īlāfi Quraysh*﴾. ﴿*riḥlata*﴾ (the journey) is the direct object of ﴿*īlāfihim*﴾. He used the singular and did not say *riḥlatay al-shitāʾ wal-ṣayf* (the two journeys of winter and summer), to avoid confusion. It is also said that ﴿*īlāfihim*﴾ is an emphasis (*taʾkīd*) of the first, not a substitute, but the first is preferable.

Abū al-Baqāʾ preferred this. It is also said that ﴿*riḥlata*﴾ is in the accusative by an implied verbal noun, meaning: their departure, the journey of winter and summer. It is also said that it is in the accusative as an adverb of time. The *riḥlah* is the departure. One of the two journeys was to Yemen in winter, because it is a hot land, and the other journey was to Syria in summer, because it is a cold land.

It has been reported that they would spend the winter (*yashtūna*) in Makkah [72] and the summer in al-Ṭāʾif.

The first view is preferable, for Quraysh's journeys for trade were known and familiar in the time of ignorance and in Islam.

Ibn Qutaybah said: Quraysh only lived by trade, and they had two journeys every year: a journey in winter to Yemen, and a journey in summer to Syria. Without these two journeys there would have been no settlement for them. And without the security granted them by their neighbourhood with the House, they would not have been able to move about freely.

﴿*Fa-l-yaʿbudū Rabba hādhā al-bayt*﴾ (So let them worship the Lord of this House). After mentioning to them what He had bestowed upon them, He, glory be to Him, commanded them to worship Him. That is: if they do not worship Him for all His other blessings, then let them worship Him for this particular blessing that has been mentioned. *Al-bayt* is the Kaʿbah.

He, glory be to Him, identified Himself to them as the Lord of this House, because they had idols which they worshipped, so He distinguished Himself from them.

It is also said that it is because through the House they were honoured above all the Arabs, so He reminded them of this as a reminder of His blessing.

﴿*Alladhī aṭʿamahum min jūʿ*﴾ (Who fed them against hunger): that is, He fed them through those two journeys against severe hunger they had been in before them. It is also said that this feeding was that when they denied the Prophet (ﷺ), he invoked against them, saying: "O Allah, make them years like the years of Yūsuf (Joseph)." So the famine intensified, and they said: "O Muḥammad, pray to Allah for us, for we are believers." So he prayed, and they became prosperous, the hunger went away, and the famine was lifted. ﴿*Wa-āmanahum min khawf*﴾ (And made them safe from fear): that is, from severe fear they had been in.

Ibn Zayd said: the Arabs used to raid one another and take each other captive, so Quraysh were safe from this because of the sanctity of the Ḥaram.

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Rabīʿ, Sharīk, and Sufyān said: He made them safe from fear of the Abyssinians with the Elephant.

Aḥmad and Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from Asmāʾ bint Yazīd, who said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: ﴿*Li-Īlāfi Quraysh*﴾ ﴿*īlāfihim riḥlata al-shitāʾ wal-ṣayf*﴾ Woe to you, O Quraysh! Worship the Lord of this House, who fed you against hunger and made you safe from fear."

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His saying ﴿*Li-Īlāfi Quraysh*﴾: "My blessing upon Quraysh." ﴿*Īlāfihim riḥlata al-shitāʾ wal-ṣayf*﴾: "They would winter in Makkah and summer in al-Ṭāʾif." ﴿*Fa-l-yaʿbudū Rabba hādhā al-bayt*﴾: "The Kaʿbah." ﴿*Alladhī aṭʿamahum min jūʿ wa-āmanahum min khawf*﴾: "The *judhām* (leprosy)."

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him also: ﴿*Li-Īlāfi Quraysh*﴾, ﴿*īlāfihim*﴾: "Their adherence (*luzūmuhum*)." ﴿*Alladhī aṭʿamahum min jūʿ*﴾: "Meaning Quraysh, the people of Makkah, by the supplication of Ibrāhīm, when he said: ﴿*And provide its people with fruits*﴾ (2:126). ﴿*Wa-āmanahum min khawf*﴾: when Ibrāhīm said: ﴿*My Lord, make this city secure*﴾ (2:126)."

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him regarding His saying ﴿*Li-Īlāfi Quraysh*﴾ to the end of the verse: "He forbade them from the journey and commanded them to worship the Lord of this House, and He would suffice them for their livelihood. Their journeys were in winter and summer, and they had no journey in winter or summer. Then Allah fed them after that against hunger and made them safe from fear, so they became accustomed to the journey, and that was among the blessings of Allah upon them."

Ibn Jarīr also narrated from him regarding the verse: "They were commanded to become accustomed to worshipping the Lord of this House, just as they had become accustomed to the journey of winter and summer." Traditions have been related about the virtue of Quraysh, and that people follow them in good and evil, and that this affair, meaning the caliphate, will remain among them as long as two of them remain. It is recorded in the registers (*dawāwīn*) of Islam.

Al-Farrāʾ said: this Surah is connected to the previous one, for He, glory be to Him, reminded the people of Makkah of His great blessing upon them in what He did to the Abyssinians. Then He said ﴿*Li-Īlāfi Quraysh*﴾, meaning: We did that to the People of the Elephant as a blessing from Us upon Quraysh. This is because Quraysh used to go out on their trade, and they were not raided in the time of ignorance (*Jāhiliyyah*), for they said: "We are the People of the House of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic." Until the owner of the Elephant came to demolish the Kaʿbah and take its stones to build with them a house in Yemen to which people would make pilgrimage; so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, destroyed them. Thus He reminded them of His blessing: that is, He did that ﴿*Li-Īlāfi Quraysh*﴾, so that they would continue to set out and no one would dare to attack them. Ibn Qutaybah mentioned something similar.

Al-Zajjāj said: the meaning is: He made them like chewed-up chaff (see 105:5) ﴿*Li-Īlāfi Quraysh*﴾, that is, Allah destroyed the People of the Elephant so that Quraysh might remain, and what they had become accustomed to of the journey of winter and summer.

Al-Zamakhsharī in *al-Kashshāf* said: the *lām* is connected to His saying ﴿*fa-l-yaʿbudū*﴾ (so let them worship), meaning: He commanded them to worship Him for the sake of their familiarity with the two journeys. The *fāʾ* (in *fa-l-yaʿbudū*) came in because the sentence carries the sense of a condition, since the meaning is: "As for whatever (it may be), let them worship Him."

Al-Khalīl ibn Aḥmad had already preceded the author of *al-Kashshāf* to this view. The meaning is: if they do not worship Him for all His other blessings, then let them worship Him for this great blessing.

Al-Kisāʾī and al-Akhfash said: the *lām* is the *lām* of wonder: that is, "Be amazed at ﴿*Li-Īlāfi Quraysh*﴾."

It is also said that it means "to" (*ilā*).

The majority of readers recited *li-īlāf*, with a *yā* and with *hamzah*, from *alifta* (ʾalifa), *yaʾlifu*, *īlāfan*.

It is said: *alifta al-shayʾ* (I was accustomed to the thing) *alafan* and *ulfan*, and *alftuhu īlāfan* has the same meaning. From it is the poet's saying:

*Those who bestow blessings when the stars have changed,*
*and those who travel on the journey of *īlāf*.*

Ibn ʿĀmir recited *li-ilāf* without the *yā*. Abū Jaʿfar recited *li-ilf*. The poet combined these two readings, saying:

*You claim that your brothers are Quraysh;*
*for them is *ilf*, and for you there is no *ilāf*.*

ʿIkrimah recited *layaʾlaf Quraysh* (let Quraysh be accustomed), with a *fatḥah* on the *lām*, taking it as the *lām* of command. It is the same in the *muṣḥaf* of Ibn Masʿūd. The *fatḥah* on the *lām* of command is a well-known dialect.

Some people of Makkah recited *ilāfu Quraysh* (with *ilāf* as a noun), and they cited the saying of Abū Ṭālib:

*He repels the people from a Hashimite band;*
*their *ilāf* among the people is the best of *ilāf*.*

Quraysh are the descendants of al-Naḍr ibn Kinānah ibn Khuzaymah ibn Mudrikah ibn Ilyās ibn Muḍar. Everyone who is a descendant of al-Naḍr is a Qurashī, and whoever is not a descendant of al-Naḍr is not a Qurashī. *Quraysh* is treated as diptote (*munṣarif*, taking nunation) if the tribe as a living group is meant, and as non-diptote (*ghayr munṣarif*, without nunation) if the tribal name is meant. From the latter is the poet's saying:

*And sufficient for Quraysh in difficult matters is its cushion.*

It is also said that Quraysh are the descendants of Fihr ibn Mālik ibn al-Naḍr, but the first view is more correct.

His saying ﴿*īlāfihim*﴾ (their familiarity) is a substitute (*badal*) for ﴿*īlāfi Quraysh*﴾. ﴿*riḥlata*﴾ (the journey) is the direct object of ﴿*īlāfihim*﴾. He used the singular and did not say *riḥlatay al-shitāʾ wal-ṣayf* (the two journeys of winter and summer), to avoid confusion. It is also said that ﴿*īlāfihim*﴾ is an emphasis (*taʾkīd*) of the first, not a substitute, but the first is preferable.

Abū al-Baqāʾ preferred this. It is also said that ﴿*riḥlata*﴾ is in the accusative by an implied verbal noun, meaning: their departure, the journey of winter and summer. It is also said that it is in the accusative as an adverb of time. The *riḥlah* is the departure. One of the two journeys was to Yemen in winter, because it is a hot land, and the other journey was to Syria in summer, because it is a cold land.

It has been reported that they would spend the winter (*yashtūna*) in Makkah [72] and the summer in al-Ṭāʾif.

The first view is preferable, for Quraysh's journeys for trade were known and familiar in the time of ignorance and in Islam.

Ibn Qutaybah said: Quraysh only lived by trade, and they had two journeys every year: a journey in winter to Yemen, and a journey in summer to Syria. Without these two journeys there would have been no settlement for them. And without the security granted them by their neighbourhood with the House, they would not have been able to move about freely.

﴿*Fa-l-yaʿbudū Rabba hādhā al-bayt*﴾ (So let them worship the Lord of this House). After mentioning to them what He had bestowed upon them, He, glory be to Him, commanded them to worship Him. That is: if they do not worship Him for all His other blessings, then let them worship Him for this particular blessing that has been mentioned. *Al-bayt* is the Kaʿbah.

He, glory be to Him, identified Himself to them as the Lord of this House, because they had idols which they worshipped, so He distinguished Himself from them.

It is also said that it is because through the House they were honoured above all the Arabs, so He reminded them of this as a reminder of His blessing.

﴿*Alladhī aṭʿamahum min jūʿ*﴾ (Who fed them against hunger): that is, He fed them through those two journeys against severe hunger they had been in before them. It is also said that this feeding was that when they denied the Prophet (ﷺ), he invoked against them, saying: "O Allah, make them years like the years of Yūsuf (Joseph)." So the famine intensified, and they said: "O Muḥammad, pray to Allah for us, for we are believers." So he prayed, and they became prosperous, the hunger went away, and the famine was lifted. ﴿*Wa-āmanahum min khawf*﴾ (And made them safe from fear): that is, from severe fear they had been in.

Ibn Zayd said: the Arabs used to raid one another and take each other captive, so Quraysh were safe from this because of the sanctity of the Ḥaram.

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Rabīʿ, Sharīk, and Sufyān said: He made them safe from fear of the Abyssinians with the Elephant.

Aḥmad and Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from Asmāʾ bint Yazīd, who said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: ﴿*Li-Īlāfi Quraysh*﴾ ﴿*īlāfihim riḥlata al-shitāʾ wal-ṣayf*﴾ Woe to you, O Quraysh! Worship the Lord of this House, who fed you against hunger and made you safe from fear."

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His saying ﴿*Li-Īlāfi Quraysh*﴾: "My blessing upon Quraysh." ﴿*Īlāfihim riḥlata al-shitāʾ wal-ṣayf*﴾: "They would winter in Makkah and summer in al-Ṭāʾif." ﴿*Fa-l-yaʿbudū Rabba hādhā al-bayt*﴾: "The Kaʿbah." ﴿*Alladhī aṭʿamahum min jūʿ wa-āmanahum min khawf*﴾: "The *judhām* (leprosy)."

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him also: ﴿*Li-Īlāfi Quraysh*﴾, ﴿*īlāfihim*﴾: "Their adherence (*luzūmuhum*)." ﴿*Alladhī aṭʿamahum min jūʿ*﴾: "Meaning Quraysh, the people of Makkah, by the supplication of Ibrāhīm, when he said: ﴿*And provide its people with fruits*﴾ (2:126). ﴿*Wa-āmanahum min khawf*﴾: when Ibrāhīm said: ﴿*My Lord, make this city secure*﴾ (2:126)."

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him regarding His saying ﴿*Li-Īlāfi Quraysh*﴾ to the end of the verse: "He forbade them from the journey and commanded them to worship the Lord of this House, and He would suffice them for their livelihood. Their journeys were in winter and summer, and they had no journey in winter or summer. Then Allah fed them after that against hunger and made them safe from fear, so they became accustomed to the journey, and that was among the blessings of Allah upon them."

Ibn Jarīr also narrated from him regarding the verse: "They were commanded to become accustomed to worshipping the Lord of this House, just as they had become accustomed to the journey of winter and summer." Traditions have been related about the virtue of Quraysh, and that people follow them in good and evil, and that this affair, meaning the caliphate, will remain among them as long as two of them remain. It is recorded in the registers (*dawāwīn*) of Islam.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (*Fath al-Qadir*) on Surah 106, verses 1–4:

It is Meccan according to the majority (*al-Jumhur*).

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and al-Kalbī said: it is Medinan.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "The Surah *Li-Īlāf* was revealed in Makkah."

Al-Bukhārī in his *Tārīkh*, al-Ṭabarānī, al-Ḥākim (who authenticated it), Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqī narrated from Umm Hānī bint Abī Ṭālib that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah has favoured Quraysh with seven qualities, which He gave to no one before them and will give to no one after them: that I am among them (and in another wording: prophethood is among them), the caliphate is among them, the custodianship of the Kaʿbah (*al-Ḥijābah*) is among them, the provision of water to the pilgrims (*al-Siqāyah*) is among them, they were granted victory over the elephant, they worshipped Allah for seven years (and in another wording: ten years) when no one else worshipped Him, and a Surah of the Qurʾān was revealed about them in which no one other than them is mentioned: *Li-Īlāfi Quraysh* [that is, the Surah of Quraysh]." Ibn Kathīr said: this is a *gharīb* (a hadith narrated through a single chain at some point). Its meaning is supported by what al-Ṭabarānī in *al-Awsaṭ*, Ibn Mardawayh, and Ibn ʿAsākir narrated from al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah has favoured Quraysh with seven qualities: He favoured them in that they worshipped Allah for ten years when none worshipped Him but Quraysh; He favoured them in that He gave them victory on the Day of the Elephant while they were polytheists; He favoured them in that a Surah of the Qurʾān was revealed about them which no one of the worlds has entered other than them, and it is *Li-Īlāfi Quraysh*; and He favoured them in that prophethood, the caliphate, and the provision of water are among them."

Al-Khaṭīb in his *Tārīkh* narrated from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab a similar report, *marfūʿ* (traced directly to the Prophet ﷺ), but it is *mursal* (a report in which the Companion is omitted from the chain).
